text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- All newspapers lead business sections with Diversified Resources Bhd group companies tripling their profit for the year to March 31. They are DRB, Gadek and Gadek Capital.
-- Independent power producer Powertron Resources Sdn Bhd has signed four agreements for the funding of its 370 million ringgit power plant in eastern Sabah state and construction of the plant.
-- Automobile distributor UMW Holdings Bhd said it has ventured into property development with a 1.2 billion ringgit project in Selangor state near Kuala Lumpur.
-- Health teams are scouring rural Sarawak, mostly in the midst of heavy tropical rainforests, for the Coxsackie B virus which has so far claimed the lives of 29 children.

-- The restructuring of the giant Bakun dam builder, Ekran Bhd will not involve group company Pacific Chemicals Bhd. "I have other plans for PCB but I cannot disclose the details," its chairman Ting Pek Khiing said.
-- Malaysia has denied reports that its companies involved in logging overseas, particularly Brazil were causing serious damage to the Amazonian forest.
-- MBf Holdings Bhd is looking to buy a bank in Thailand, its chairman Loy Hean Heong said. This follows a failed attempt by group firm MBf Capital to obtain permission to take over Suria Capital.
